title: VLAN Configuration, Part 1: Create VLANs and Assign Ports
labSub: Create VLANs and put ports in them

scenes.narration: Welcome to the VLAN configuration series. In part one, we start with a brand new switch and nothing else. By the end, one switch will behave like two completely separate networks. Here's what you'll do. First, you'll look at a fresh switch and see where every port starts. Next, you'll create two V L A Ns and give them sensible names. Then you'll move the right ports into the right V L A N. Finally, you'll check your work, and avoid one classic mistake.

items.t: Look at a brand new switch and spot the default VLAN
Create two VLANs and give them names
Move the right ports into each VLAN
Check your work and avoid a classic mistake

scenes.heading: The idea in 20 seconds
scenes.narration: Before we type anything, let's lock in the idea. Think of the switch as an apartment building. Each V L A N is a separate floor. Each port is a flat's front door. Mail never leaves its own floor, unless a router carries it.

items.story: A port is a front door

scenes.narration: We're connected to the console of switch S W one, in privileged mode. Let's start by looking at what a fresh switch gives us, with show V L A N brief. Every single port is sitting in V L A N one, called default. That means all four computers can talk to each other, and that's what we're about to change.

steps.note: show vlan brief lists every VLAN and its ports.

out: 1    default             active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4

steps.note: A new switch puts every port in VLAN 1.
Today's goal: split them into two groups.

scenes.narration: Step one is to create the V L A Ns. First we enter global configuration mode. Then we create V L A N ten, and give it a name. We do the same for V L A N twenty, which will be for engineering. Pressing end takes us straight back out, and show V L A N brief confirms both exist.

out: Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.

steps.note: vlan 10 creates it; name labels it.
Same again for the second floor.
Both VLANs exist, but no ports are in them yet.

out: 1    default             active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4

scenes.narration: Step two is to put the ports into those V L A Ns. We select fast ethernet one and two together, using the range command. We set them to access mode, which means one V L A N, for an ordinary computer. And we put them in V L A N ten. Now the engineering ports. Fast ethernet three and four go to V L A N twenty. Back to the top with end, and show V L A N brief shows the finished result.

steps.note: range lets you configure several ports at once.
Access mode: this port serves one VLAN.
This is the line that actually assigns the VLAN.
Ports 1-2 are in SALES, 3-4 in ENGINEERING.

out: 1    default             active    Fa0/5, Fa0/6, Fa0/7, Fa0/8

scenes.narration: A good engineer always verifies. Show interfaces fast ethernet zero slash one switchport tells us exactly how one port is set. Static access, and V L A N ten called sales. Exactly what we wanted. And here is the classic mistake. If you assign a port to a V L A N that doesn't exist, the switch creates it for you. Always run show V L A N brief afterwards, so a typo can't hide.

steps.note: This command shows one port's VLAN settings.
It's in VLAN 10, as an access port.
A typo here silently makes a new VLAN.

out: % Access VLAN does not exist. Creating vlan 30

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three things to remember from this part. Every port starts in V L A N one. Creating a V L A N and assigning ports are two separate steps. And a mistyped V L A N number quietly creates a new one.

items.right: Every new switch port is in VLAN 1
Creating a VLAN and assigning ports are two steps
A wrong VLAN number creates a new VLAN

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Create the V L A N with vlan, then name it. Put ports in with switchport mode access and switchport access vlan. And always check with show V L A N brief. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva VLAN lab.
